items.evidence: Three independent dead causes, all javap-verified against the 26.1 jar. (1) Dead dispatch: Class::Speleothem = "SpeleothemBlock" (level/classes.rs:215) gates five dispatch sites (place.rs:1156, shapes.rs:728, survive.rs:307, tick.rs:248, tick.rs:434), but there is NO SpeleothemBlock class in 26.1 - PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly (the 1.21.7 shape) and its prepared class chain is [PointedDripstoneBlock, Block], so no Speleothem arm ever fires. (2) Dead tag: speleothem_tag() reads #minecraft:speleothems, absent from 26.1 data (no tag file, no BlockTags.SPELEOTHEMS field, no key in prepared block-tags.json), so speleothem_with / speleothem_is_tip / is_free_hanging_stalactite / speleothem_unmerged_tip are always false and falling.rs:55 spawn_falling_stalactite is tag-gated. (3) Missing link: prepared fields for pointed_dripstone is {} (no blockToGrowOn), so data.link is None and speleothem_grow's can_grow is always false; vanilla 26.1 PDB.canGrow hardcodes Blocks.DRIPSTONE_BLOCK + water source at above(2). Vanilla PDB bytecode (1716 lines) has ZERO BlockTags references - all predicates are same-block. Observable: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, placement, updateShape, canSurvive (falls through to true, floating dripstone never breaks), scheduled tick, falling stalactite spawn all dead. NOT dead: fallOn stalagmite damage and trident break (name/data-keyed). The dead-code constants in speleothem.rs match vanilla exactly but were not counted as passes. Reproduces pilot G6 + B11-G06.
items.title: Entire pointed-dripstone system dead (no SpeleothemBlock class, no #speleothems tag, no blockToGrowOn link)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 FallingBlockEntity.tick runs the landing branch at the first water cell (onGround || inWater, where inWater = concrete powder && fluid is WATER tag, with a fast-fall clip check using ClipContext.Block.COLLIDER + ClipContext.Fluid.SOURCE_ONLY); the port's game/falling_blocks.rs fall_step has no concrete-powder water check at all and game/falling_damage.rs finish_falling_block always passes stuck_in_water=false, so powder sinks to the lakebed. The horizon-world landing branch itself (level/falling.rs falling_block_landed) matches vanilla, including the onLand replaced-state check - the fix is local to the client fall step. Carries over from pilot G2. Same defect as 26.2's B1-G02.
items.title: Concrete powder falling into water does not solidify on contact

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 AbstractThrownPotion.onHitBlock gates on PotionContents.is(Potions.WATER) - Holder equality, NOT a tag. The port's game/splash_water.rs ships the 26.3 tag form: potion_in_tag(stack, "minecraft:douses_fire" / "hurts_water_sensitive_entities" / "extinguishes_entities" / "rehydrates_axolotls"), read from trades.potion_tags built from the prepared data's tags/potion directory (merchant.rs:488-489, 574). That directory contains ONLY tradeable.json in 26.1 (verified in the client jar and in prepared data), so all four gates are always closed and no splash water ever dowses fire, hurts water-sensitive entities, extinguishes burning entities, or rehydrates axolotls. 26.2's file uses is_water_potion (Potions.WATER equality) and works. The downstream code matches vanilla exactly (dowse targets, dowseFire, the (4,2,4) box, dist^2<16, hurt 1.0 indirectMagic, axolotl +1800 air capped) but is unreachable. Reproduces B11-G13.
items.title: Splash water never douses fire / hurts / extinguishes / rehydrates (potion tags are 26.3-only)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 EntityFluidInteraction is the 26.2 form (javap-verified): trackerByFluid Map<TagKey, Tracker> with the current ON the tracker, no CurrentAccumulator class, update returns void; the eye check uses the PLAIN top (y + FluidState.getHeight). The port's horizon-world/src/entity_fluid.rs ships the 26.3 form (per-kind trackers + separate CurrentAccumulators, update returns Result<bool>) and its eye check (entity_fluid.rs:389-398) computes the top with world.camera_height(state, p) (fluid.rs:504 camera_height_at: a source fluid with a sturdy block above -> 1.0, else height_at). Observable: an entity whose eye is in (0.889, 1.0] above a source's block bottom with a solid ceiling -> the port says eyes-in-fluid, vanilla 26.1 says not; affects was_eye_in_water / is_under_water (swimming, overlay, air/drowning). The rest of the 26.3 form was verified behaviourally equivalent for vanilla fluids (flow scaling, fluid_height/is_in_fluid/is_eye_in_fluid, tracker pruning; the update bool return differs only in a 1mm band and all callers discard it).
items.title: Entity fluid interaction eye check uses camera height instead of the plain fluid top

items.evidence: Batch 0 measurement (docs/sweep/26.1/batch-0-oracles.json): three oracles fail on the same missing symbol, BlockTags.BLOCKS_FLUID_FLOW - VanillaFluidFlowOracle (1 error, line 15), VanillaRegisteredEntityFluidOracle (2 errors, lines 9-10), VanillaRegistryFluidOracle (3 errors, lines 11, 14; line 17 is B1-O04's symbol). javap-verified: BlockTags has no BLOCKS_FLUID_FLOW field in the 26.1 server-game jar - it is a 26.3-only tag (this batch's own tag inventory confirms blocks_fluid_flow does not exist in 26.1's data). Same as 26.2 B1-O01. The port deliberately maps blocks_fluid_flow := blocks_motion for 26.1, so the repair is to bind the tag from the blocks_motion table, not to add the tag.
items.title: Three fluid oracles do not compile for 26.1: BlockTags.BLOCKS_FLUID_FLOW is 26.3-only (FluidFlow, RegisteredEntityFluid, RegistryFluid)

method: javap -c on the named 26.1 server-game jar (DataVersion 4786, protocol 775, Java 25) for every vanilla method in scope, plus Rust source comparison against versions/26.1/crates/, tag/data reads from the 26.1 client jar and the 26.1 datagen reports, the prepared data at versions/26.1/.local/horizon-client/26.1/ (GATE OK, landed before the run), and oracle triage from the measured Batch 0 table (docs/sweep/26.1/batch-0-oracles.json) only. No cargo builds, no unit tests, no fresh oracle measurement (brief constraints).
name: Fluids + falling blocks
out_of_scope_failures: None. Untraced sub-details (not counted as passes, not needs-harness): the lava-hurt GENERIC_BURN sound was not traced in the Rust; PointedDripstoneBlock.animateTick drip particles were not compared; dragon-egg teleport on use is out of scope (falling-block scope covers fall/landing/conversion) - though it was verified matching anyway (1000 tries, same offsets and gates). Oracle triage: 9 of the 13 in-scope oracles fail on all three classpaths (B1-O01..B1-O07); the other 4 pass (FluidBox, FluidOccupancy, FluidShape, WaterSplash - all three classpaths).
source: 26.1 parity sweep, batch 1 - the 1.21.7 pilot scope re-run against vanilla 26.1 (checks only, no fixes). Scope: water/lava spreading and flow, fluid pushing, bubble columns, concrete powder solidification, lava fire spread + ignition + game rules, dripstone growth + cauldron fill, falling blocks, cauldron fill levels, splash water. Re-checks all six 1.21.7 pilot defects (G1-G6) and Batch 11 findings B11-G06, B11-G13 against 26.1's own jar/data.
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 pilot's systemic root cause (26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in the target version's data) DOES apply to 26.1 again, in two places: the speleothem system (B1-G01: #speleothems and SpeleothemBlock both absent - 26.1 has the 1.21.7 PointedDripstoneBlock shape, not 26.2's) and splash water (B1-G03: the four potion tags absent, only tradeable exists). Where 26.1's data HAS the tag (bubble-column tags, #signs, #fire, #anvil, infiniburn), the port reads it; where 26.1 still lacks the tag, the port usually carries the hardcoded 1.21.7-style list form - except in those two places, where it ships the 26.3 form. B1-G04 is the same pattern at a smaller scale (26.3-form entity fluid interaction, camera-height eye check). Three of six pilot defects and neither Batch 11 finding are closed for 26.1; G2, G6, B11-G06, B11-G13 reproduce; G4 is not applicable as framed (no doFireTick rule in 26.1 - 59 gamerules by javap).
